correctness.rationale: The Fourier coefficient identity is obtained by direct integration and cosine frequency shifts. Every admissibility inequality is converted exactly to an adjacent-coefficient ratio; frequency zero is strictly dominated. The ratio has one unique positive continuous minimizer, giving at most four integer candidates. Strictness follows from eventual positivity and a Vandermonde argument. Both asymptotics and the infinitely many uniquely active indices have analytic derivative/Taylor proofs. CHECK.py reproduces independent finite diagnostics, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Signed harmonic perturbations of a geodesic Laplace covariance are natural for circular stationary models. Unlike closure-based nonnegative-mixture constructions, the sharp allowable negative cosine coefficient is not evident from positivity of the baseline. The result replaces infinitely many Fourier inequalities with at most four and discovers an unbounded staircase of active spectral constraints, giving a usable exact admissibility rule and a nontrivial scale-frequency transition, not a routine fixed-parameter check.
